labels.wall_m: PROTOTYPE (the 5 mm skin of Vertex 2.6, class "bare")

regimes: Below about 3 km/s the grain stays mostly whole and digs a crater.
From about 3 km/s the shock breaks the grain into fragments: the speed range Whipple shields are built for.
From about 7 km/s grain and bumper melt where they meet.
From about 20 km/s they turn to vapour.
From about 100 km/s the impact makes a plasma: dust detectors on spacecraft count grains by that charge.
Above about 1,000 km/s each atom arrives with tens of keV: more like a burst of ion beam than a collision. No laboratory has made such an impact with a grain.
regime_sources: Whipple-shield fragmentation, melt and vapour onset near 3, 7 and 20 km/s (hypervelocity-impact literature, e.g. Piekutowski; NASA HVIT); impact-plasma dust detectors (Galileo, Ulysses, Cassini CDA); electrostatic dust accelerators reach about 100 km/s for sub-micron grains; the regime above 1,000 km/s is an EXTRAPOLATION
speeds: typical orbital-debris strike; Whipple shields are tested here
the fastest a meteor from the solar system can reach Earth
Giotto flew through Halley's dust in 1986 behind a 1 mm bumper
electrostatic dust accelerators, sub-micron grains only

phases.name: accelerate out
phases.text: Bow first, faster every day: out of the inner solar system and through the Kuiper belt's dust, where most grains get through the Brow's layer.

phases.name: flip before braking (destination)
phases.text: A 300 s turn at full speed: for a moment the whole side of the ship faces the dust.

phases.name: brake at destination
phases.text: Engines first: the four engine fronts now lead into the dust.

phases.name: accelerate home
phases.text: Bow first again, in thin outer dust.

phases.name: flip before braking (home)
phases.text: The second turn at full speed.

phases.name: brake at home
phases.text: Engines first, braking back through the Kuiper belt into the inner solar system: the engine fronts' worst stretch.

LOW: the low end of the published measurements
NOMINAL: the published measurements at their central values
JUSTIFIED: every measured input at its upper bound and every untested damage rule at its worst (Vertex 2.7; proposed design envelope, owner decision open)
HIGH: adds what nobody has measured: Kuiper-belt grains up to 1 g and the disputed radar flux of large interstellar grains. A conditional safety gate, not a design case

proto.stack: disruptor layer 5 mm C/C, skin 5 mm (thicknesses OPEN in canon)
proto.visual_rates: sparks on the page stand for many grains each; the counters are the model numbers
